The Live Nation Labs fund he helped run targeted early-stage startups in consumer product development and tech infrastructure.

brief.headline: Michael Abrams has spent his career evaluating, incubating, investing in and acquiring entertainment tech at Live Nation, so a live-events app that extends the ticket into a full night out is squarely in his world.
brief.angle: Frame the startup as consumer product and tech infrastructure that adds value around the ticket: pre-show bars, merch and rides, tuned to each fanbase. Show it as something a strategic partner like Live Nation could plug into or learn from, with early traction and a clear view of how it works alongside ticketing rather than against it.
deck: Open with the problem: a ticket gets someone in the door, but the night around the show is fragmented and unplanned.
Show the product early, with one concert walked through from pre-show bar to merch to ride home.
Explain how picks are personalized per fanbase and why that makes each event feel built for that crowd.
Present your 25 to 29 year old core audience with any usage data you have, labeled clearly as yours.
Add a slide on how you fit with ticketing platforms, and what a strategic partner would gain from integration or data.
avoid: Do not position the app as a Ticketmaster replacement, since his background is inside the live-events ecosystem and partnership is the likelier path.
Do not assume his current stage or check size, because public sources only confirm early-stage focus from his earlier Live Nation Labs work.
Do not cite portfolio companies or personal interests as common ground, since none were confirmed in the research.
questions: How do you make money per user: ticket-linked commission, merch margin, ride referrals, or something else?
Why would venues, promoters or ticketing platforms work with you instead of building this themselves?
How do you get the first users for each fanbase, and what does repeat use look like beyond one concert?
